questions.question_text: Find the general primitive function $f(x)$ given $f'(x)=4x^{3}+3$.

options.why: Left the constant term $3$ unchanged instead of finding its primitive $3x$.
Raised the power of $x^{3}$ but did not divide its coefficient by the new power $4$.
Differentiated $4x^{3}+3$ instead of finding its primitive.
Raised each power by $1$ but did not divide by the new powers.
Divided by the original powers $2$ and $1$ instead of the new powers $3$ and $2$.
Differentiated the given function instead of finding its primitive.
Raised the power but did not divide the coefficient $10$ by the new power $10$.
Differentiated $10x^{9}$ instead of finding its primitive.
Divided the coefficient by $10$ but left the power at $9$.

questions.question_text: Find the general primitive function $f(x)$ given $f'(x)=14x$.

options.why: Omitted the constant of integration, so this names only one primitive rather than the whole family.
Attached the constant to $x$; differentiating this gives $14x+C$, not $14x$.
Added $C$ to the given derivative without finding its primitive.

questions.question_text: Find the general primitive of $(3x-2)(x+5)$ after expanding.

options.why: Expanded correctly but omitted the primitive $-10x$ of the constant term $-10$.
Used $+2x$ instead of $-2x$ when expanding, giving the incorrect middle term $17x$.
Expanded correctly and raised the powers, but did not divide the first two terms by their new powers.

questions.question_text: Find the general primitive function $h(x)$ given $h'(x)=0$.

options.why: Gave only one primitive instead of including every constant function.
Treated the zero derivative as $1$; the derivative of $x+C$ is $1$.
Found the primitive of $x$ instead of the primitive of $0$.

questions.question_text: Write $\dfrac{4}{x^{3}}$ using a negative power of $x$. Then find its general primitive, writing it as a fraction without a negative index.

options.why: Divided by $2$ instead of the new power $-2$, losing the negative sign.
Raised the power to $-2$ but divided by the original power $-3$.
Differentiated $4x^{-3}$ instead of finding its primitive.

questions.question_text: Find the general primitive of $x^{3}(6x^{4}+5)$ after expanding.

options.why: Found the primitive of $6x^{7}$ but left the term $5x^{3}$ unchanged.
Expanded correctly and raised the powers, but did not divide by the new powers $8$ and $4$.
Divided by the original powers $7$ and $3$ instead of the new powers $8$ and $4$.
